cohort: 25,279 privately insured women in Iowa who gave birth
finding: This study found that postpartum women with mood and anxiety disorders were more likely to fill opioid prescriptions within the first 3 months postpartum, regardless of delivery mode.
mod_finding: The presence of mood and anxiety disorders increased the odds of filling at least one opioid prescription by 20% among women with cesarean deliveries, compared to a 50% increase among women with vaginal deliveries.
